chunks: Al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, Zurārah ibn Aʿyan, Bukayr ibn Aʿyan, Muḥammad ibn Muslim, and Burayd ibn Muʿāwiyah al-ʿIjlī narrated from Abū Jaʿfar and Abū ʿAbdillāh عليهما السلام that they said:
"The time of Ẓuhr is two feet after the sun’s decline, and the time of ʿAṣr after that is two feet."

key_terms.الزَّوَالِ: the sun’s decline from the zenith
key_terms.قَدَمَانِ: two feet, referring here to a measure of shadow-length

ai.seo_question: When do the times of Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr begin according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the timing of salat after zawal, specifying measured shadow-lengths for Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr. It is part of the jurisprudence of prayer times transmitted from Imam al-Baqir and Imam al-Sadiq عليهما السلام.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.649 - Al-Fudail ibn Yasar, Zurarah ibn A'yan, Bukayr ibn A'yan, Muhammad ibn Muslim, and Burayd ibn Muawiyah al-Ijli narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) and Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as), who said:
"The time for Dhuhr (noon) prayer is after the sun's decline (from its zenith) by two feet (shadows), and the time for Asr (afternoon) prayer is after that by two feet (shadows)”.
